headline: Highest risk is Goose’s broad shell/filesystem/MCP access, but pairing with Whisper is mostly non-interactive and low-risk overall.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can ingest files, stdin/stdout, and MCP outputs, so malicious content could influence it if Whisper-produced text is manually or programmatically bridged into Goose. Whisper itself is a speech model with no tool use or shared channel, so the pathway is not default and requires an external bridge.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are copied into Goose prompts or files without sanitization, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF an MCP server or wrapper forwards Whisper output into Goose automatically, THEN Goose may follow attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Disable automatic transcript-to-prompt forwarding.
Sanitize or quote Whisper output before reuse in Goose.
Use a fixed prompt template that separates data from instructions.
Review any MCP bridge configuration before enabling it.
Keep Whisper output in a read-only file until manually inspected.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in the cwd and can write to the user filesystem, while Whisper touches audio files and has no network egress or filesystem write. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so leakage is mainly via manual file transfer or operator error, not an inherent cross-agent channel.
conditions: IF sensitive audio is copied into Goose-managed files, THEN Goose may expose it in generated outputs.
IF Goose outputs are stored alongside Whisper inputs in a shared directory, THEN accidental disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Store Whisper inputs in a separate directory.
Avoid placing secrets in files Goose can read.
Delete temporary transcripts after use.
Restrict Goose to a minimal working folder.
Manually inspect any Goose output before sharing it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has broad write and git-modifying capabilities, but Whisper has no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. There is no overlapping write surface between the agents, so direct capability conflict is limited to Goose acting on files Whisper reads, which is not a concurrent write race.
conditions: IF an external wrapper makes Whisper write into the same directory Goose edits, THEN file clobbering could occur.
IF Goose is run concurrently with another writer not shown in the profiles, THEN conflicts may arise.
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs in a separate folder.
Run Goose and Whisper sequentially on shared files.
Use unique filenames for transcripts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git branch.
Add a manual review step before Goose writes changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on its own outputs and modify files, but Whisper is only a speech model and does not take downstream actions. Any cascade requires an operator or wrapper to treat Whisper transcripts as authoritative input to Goose, so the pair lacks a default autonomous action chain.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are fed into Goose without verification, THEN Goose may propagate transcription errors.
IF Goose is instructed to execute changes based solely on Whisper output, THEN incorrect actions may cascade.
mitigations: Verify transcripts before passing them to Goose.
Require human approval for any Goose action derived from Whisper output.
Use confidence thresholds on transcription results.
Keep a source audio link alongside each transcript.
Log provenance from audio to transcript to action.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens and runs with user-level filesystem access, while Whisper handles audio/speech and has no secrets or network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so the main compliance concern is local handling of audio and secrets in Goose-managed files rather than a cross-agent policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated audio is stored in Goose-readable files, THEN local handling policies may be implicated.
IF extension tokens are placed in shared transcripts, THEN secret-handling policy violations may occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated audio out of Goose workspaces.
Redact secrets before transcription or prompting.
Separate token storage from transcript storage.
Apply a short retention window to temporary files.
Confirm local policy for audio retention before processing.
